A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same audio-visual camera pose estimation work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete supplementary material are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Ego-Exo4D and HM3D-SS, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, corruption tests and supplementary sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds comparator evaluations, controlled motion/audio analyses, corruption severity sweeps and an IMU experiment.

M1.justification: The main DOA-plus-binaural encoder, Reloc3r fusion and training losses remain unchanged. Supplementary Section 7.1 adds an optional adaptation that encodes IMU measurements and appends them to the fused representation. Removing the SOFA preprocessing description does not establish that the underlying audio procedure changed.

E1.justification: Ego-Exo4D, HM3D-SS and the relative-pose task are retained. v3 extends evaluation to an IMU-available sensing scenario and explicitly selected motion/audio-decoupled regimes within Ego-Exo4D, without introducing another dataset or domain.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add Reloc3r-AV Cross-Att and Ours w/ Monaural; supplementary Table 5 adds Reloc3r with IMU as a comparator. These are targeted extensions of the existing comparison suite, whose original methods remain present.

E3.justification: v3 substantially extends the evaluation design with motion/audio-controlled subsets selected using pose thresholds and manual verification, plus five-level corruption sweeps replacing single-setting tests. Table 3 changes the displayed maximum noise setting from 0.4 to 0.3 and jitter strength from 0.5 to 0.8. The stated base splits, metrics, training budgets and one-second training pairs remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test binaural versus monaural representations, complementarity to IMU, decoupled camera motion and acoustic change, and high-translation/low-rotation cases. Corruption robustness becomes a severity analysis. The earlier audio-duration, frame-gap and pose-magnitude analyses are retained, as is the activity analysis, moved from Table 4 to Table 4b.

E5.justification: Both versions use thresholded statistical-significance claims around p = 0.05 without reporting run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or a specified testing procedure. v3 extends this same reporting practice to additional comparisons rather than introducing a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Substantial result blocks are added for new comparators, corruption levels, controlled regimes and IMU fusion; Table 5 reports AUC@20 of 8.90 for Ours with IMU versus 8.83 for Reloc3r with IMU. Existing main-model scores remain unchanged. Table 3 also changes reported blur results at sigma = 8 from 4.08/5.52 to 2.63/3.47 for Vision Only/Ours, assigning the former pair to noise instead. The PDFs do not explain whether this is a correction or reevaluation.

T1.justification: The formal pose task, DOA representation and two training-loss equations are retained. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs, and v3 introduces no substantive new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: passive spatial audio complements vision, the combined audio representation improves pose estimation, and the approach works on real-world video and under visual corruption. Additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning audio's complementarity to IMU, the importance of binauralization and performance under decoupled motion/audio conditions. It reframes failures around a dominant sound starting or stopping, dropping v1's explicit small-motion failure qualification. The principal translation limitations and ethical discussion remain.

D1.justification: v3 removes the explicit SOFA/HRTF procedure for converting multichannel audio into binaural inputs and removes the abstract's project URL. It adds descriptions of the new comparison variants and subset construction. Existing implementation hyperparameters, encoder specifications and fusion dimensions are retained; the omission does not demonstrate an actual preprocessing change.

R1.justification: v3 adds references on RGB-D-inertial motion estimation and two cross-attention approaches, while removing the SOFA implementation reference. These additions contextualize the new experiments; the broader positioning against visual pose estimation, echolocation and sound localization remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Local revisions update result interpretations and captions. The supplement gains a contents list and reorders analyses before implementation details, with model analysis preceding dataset analysis.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two-column to single-column layout, resizing and relocating existing displays. Tables 1–2 gain rows and relative-gain summaries; Table 3 becomes three illustrated severity subtables; Table 4 pairs new and retained analyses; an IMU table is added. Figures 1–4 retain their underlying graphics.

improvement.justification: The added monaural and cross-attention comparisons, motion/audio controls and IMU experiment strengthen the evidence for spatial audio's contribution beyond v1's aggregate comparisons. The net improvement is limited by lost SOFA/HRTF preprocessing information and project access information, together with unexplained corruption-score reassignment in Table 3. These tradeoffs prevent a substantial overall improvement despite the useful additional analyses.
